author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Cholera continues to kill thousands across Africa annually, particularly in communities lacking clean water and sanitation, despite being a preventable waterborne disease. South Africa's BioVac Institute is developing an oral cholera vaccine that, once approved, would be the first end-to-end African-produced cholera vaccine in over 50 years. Global cholera vaccine supply has doubled from 35 million doses in 2022 to 70 million in 2023, yet experts emphasise vaccination alone cannot stop cholera without coordinated efforts including access to clean water, sanitation facilities and healthcare. Africa currently produces less than 1 per cent of vaccines used on the continent, with the African CDC aiming to increase this to 60 per cent by 2040.

Al Jazeera's Fahmida Miller reports from Cape Town, South Africa.

Syria's government has been conducting an operation to take control of areas held by the Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces in the country's north, though it has yet to deploy forces in the strategic city of Kobani. More than 100 PKK fighters, designated a terrorist organisation by the EU and Turkey, were granted safe passage out of the area on Monday, but hundreds more are believed to remain. Whilst an integration agreement is in place and internal security forces have replaced the military in some towns, many Kurds fear the consequences of government control. Damascus insists national unity is essential for post-war recovery, with Kobani serving as a critical test of whether integration can be achieved through negotiation rather than force.

Al Jazeera's Teresa Bo reports from Birek, northern Syria.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Ali Larijani, Iran’s Supreme National Security Council secretary, told Al Jazeera in Doha that Tehran is negotiating only with the United States and accused Israel of trying to sabotage the process.
His remarks follow mediated US-Iran talks in Oman that ended without a breakthrough and no new round scheduled.
Larijani alleged Israel seeks regional destabilisation involving states including Qatar, Saudi Arabia and Turkey.
Iranian officials cite last year’s Israeli strike before planned talks as a source of deep mistrust.
Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi also referenced that incident as evidence diplomacy was undermined.
Tehran says it will negotiate solely on its nuclear programme, limited to uranium enrichment levels.
Washington, including President Donald Trump, wants broader talks covering missiles and regional allies, highlighting a major gap.

Al Jazeera’s Resul Serdar reports from Tehran, Iran.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Israeli settlers have demolished Palestinian homes in the occupied West Bank, operating alongside Israeli soldiers in Area C, where Palestinians are barred from building. 
Unlike typical demolitions carried out by the Israeli military, settlers used bulldozers to destroy structures—some without demolition notices—and reportedly stole property. 
The UN says settler attacks have displaced hundreds of Palestinians since the start of the year, part of what Palestinians describe as a policy of impunity. 
The demolitions follow recent Israeli government decisions that would permit settlers to expand into Palestinian areas across the West Bank.

Al Jazeera's Nidha Ibrahim reports from the occupied West Bank.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
A Chadian chemist and a British activist devoted their lives to the Palestinian resistance but paid the ultimate price.

Bashir Jibril, born in Jerusalem to a Chadian family, joined the Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine (PFLP) after the 1967 Arab-Israeli war. He trained military cadres and took part in the 1970 airliner hijackings, before being killed in a car bomb explosion in Athens in 1978.

Faris Glubb, also born in Jerusalem, is the son of Glubb Pasha, a British military General who commanded the Arab Legion between 1939 and 1956. Faris joined Fatah, then the Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine [PFLP], but later moved to the Palestine Liberation Front [PLF] and lived under constant threat for his activism. He was the first person to introduce the idea of using paragliders to the PLF’s military wing. A journalist and a dedicated activist, he documented the relationship between Zionism and Nazism. He died on 3 April 2004 in a mysterious car accident in Kuwait.
title: The story of two Jerusalem-born activists who died for Palestine | Al Jazeera World Documentary

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Police in Canada have identified an 18-year-old woman as the suspect in a school shooting that killed eight people, including the gunman's mother and stepbrother.
Jesse Van Rootselaar killed a teacher and five students, aged 12 to 14, at Tumbler Ridge Secondary School in British Columbia before dying of a self-inflicted gunshot wound.
Twenty-seven others were wounded. Authorities say they have not yet established a motive, and police had previously responded to mental health and weapons calls at the shooter's home.
Mass shootings are rare in Canada, which has strict gun control laws.
The small town of Tumbler Ridge, home to around 2,700 people, has been plunged into mourning, with residents coming together to grieve the loss of community members.

Al Jazeera's Heidi Zhou-Castro reports.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Polls have opened in Bangladesh's first election since mass protests toppled Sheikh Hasina in 2024, with nearly 127 million registered voters choosing between the Bangladesh National Party and Jamaat-e-Islami. 
Voters are also casting ballots in a constitutional referendum on reforms designed to prevent a return to autocracy. 
Key issues include corruption, unemployment, pollution and law-and-order concerns following post-uprising unrest. 
Security is tight, with more than 50 parties competing in what is seen as a crucial test of Bangladesh's return to democracy.

Al Jazeera's Jonah Hull reports from Dhaka, Bangladesh.

Democratic lawmakers have grilled United States Attorney General Pam Bondi over her handling of the files pertaining to convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, during a combative hearing before the House Judiciary Committee.
Wednesday’s hearing was entitled “Oversight of the US Department of Justice”, but the Epstein files quickly became a primary focus.
“ As attorney general, you are siding with the perpetrators, and you’re ignoring the victims,” Democrat Jamie Raskin told Bondi at the outset.
“That will be your legacy unless you act quickly to change course. You’re running a massive Epstein cover-up right out of the Department of Justice.”
Since the start of his second term, US President Donald Trump and his administration have consistently faced questions about the decision to withhold or redact documents related to Epstein.
